pages.title: Blank Classifier
pages.text: $(bold)The OBSR prototype$() is an untrained blank classifier. It has no function of its own, only a writable record table.$(br2)The recipe is shapeless.

$(bold)Procedure:$()$(br2)$(li)1. Place the prototype in the $(bold)Training Terminal$() and choose OBSR-2 or OBSR-1 as the training direction.$(br)$(li)2. Take the prototype back out.$(br)$(li)3. Right-click blocks or creatures with the prototype to record their readings into it.
pages.title: Procedure

pages.text: $(li)4. Repeat recording until the table is full or you judge it sufficient.$(br)$(li)5. Return the prototype to the terminal and finish training.$(br2)The record table has a capacity limit. Duplicate entries do not count.
pages.title: Procedure (cont.)

pages.text: $(bold)Concept resolution:$() On completion of training the terminal identifies a $(bold)concept$() from the record table and computes completeness q. The concept is taken from the corpus tag with the highest coverage.
pages.title: Concept Resolution

pages.text: q = the number of entries in the record table belonging to that concept, divided by the total number of members of that concept.$(br2)When there are too few entries within the concept, the terminal judges it an $(bold)incomplete classification$(): the model is invalid and must be retrained.
$(bold)Appendix: Experiment Records$()$(br2)The following are three repeat runs of the same training set in the previous iteration. The record table held the same number of entries each time.
pages.title: Appendix: Experiment Records

pages.text: $(li)Record table: 8 entries, all members of one concept$(br)$(li)Completeness q: 0.25$(br)$(li)Note: model valid, guidance limited to that concept.
$(li)Record table: 8 entries, 5 belonging to concept A and 3 to concept B$(br)$(li)Completeness q: 0.16$(br)$(li)Note: concept A is taken as it has the higher coverage; range is limited.
$(li)Record table: 8 entries across 6 concepts$(br)$(li)Completeness q: 0$(br)$(li)Note: judged an incomplete classification; model invalid.

$(bold)Conclusion:$() q measures how thoroughly the record table covers a single concept, independently of the number of entries.$(br2)When training OBSR-1, concentrate the records on one and the same concept.
$(bold)Record retention:$() A trained model can be duplicated by recipe; the copy retains every record, the concept and q.$(br2)OBSR-3 is not among the models that can be duplicated.
